lede: You asked for every page beyond the homepage to be redesigned in the new system and restructured before anything goes live (round 7, C7). Here are all sixteen as mockups. Each one answers the question a buyer has at that point, shows the work instead of describing it, and ends at one of the two doors: the audit, or the team.
checked: Each page was built from the story map, then read by a second designer the way you would read it, then fixed. All of them pass the same build checks as the homepage mockups.

sequence: What exactly would you build in my company, and what would I hold?
Is a company like mine what you're for?
Who is behind this, and can I trust them?
Do they think clearly about my problem?
Show me proof. What do I actually get?
What does the first step ask of me, and how do I start?
I'm not ready, or I need something specific.
Are they hiring? Are they a software company? What happens to my data?
rules: Your approved header, on every page
The Specimen-sheet header from round 3, without its title block: a two-voice headline, three facts, and one drawing of what the page is about. The drawing is different on every page.
Each page shows one thing only it has, such as a page of the document a layer delivers, the ten audit days to scale, or the rules the firm runs by.
Every page ends at a door
The audit for the ready, the team for everyone else. There are five kinds of close, so the endings never read as a template.
Red buttons lead only to /audit, and none sit in a header. Contact and Careers have no red at all. Each page has one paper section, its one change of surface.
Specimens are labelled and hold no client data. Anything not yet true says so: “In development”, “Drafting”, “Not yet published”, “None yet”.
At most two third-party figures per page, each with its source linked and its wording careful.

pages.signature: The break chart: the same three layers drawn once for each situation, with a fracture where each one breaks first.
flags: The markets section is headed “The same three situations, in six markets”, but no market line names a situation, and five of the six break in the narrative layer. Keep the heading, or retitle it “Where it breaks, by market”?

“Seven stakeholders” is cut from the first market line, because it had no source.

pages.name: About
pages.question: “Who is actually behind this, can I trust them with my revenue system, and how would they work with us?”
pages.story: The person who signed the homepage letter, next to the five rules the firm runs by. The rules are drawn first on the method's own timeline, then written out in full on paper, then shown as the week an engagement runs on. Then the first step.
pages.signature: Where the five rules bind: a matrix on the method's time axis, then the rules in full.
flags: “Led by · Rameez, Founder · Lead Narrative Architect”, “Based · London”, and “The firm today · One architect; the next seat, a Systems Engineer” (Q1).
No background line under your name and no portrait, unless you give one (Q1).
The week (Monday signal review through Friday's written note) stays only if that's how your engagements run (Q7).
The lede says the firm builds “revenue systems that its clients keep”, which can read as if installs have already run. The careful version: “revenue systems the client keeps after handover” (Q2).

pages.name: Insights
pages.question: “Does this firm think clearly about my problem, and is there something I can read before I talk to anyone?”
pages.story: It lands on the letter's “Field notes, published”. A register shows which layer each note diagnoses, one note is offered to read first, and everything still being written is listed with an honest status. The research documents that sat on /reports move here.
pages.signature: The register: each note set against the layer it diagnoses.
flags: Read times stay at 6, 5 and 5 minutes to match the homepage, though the notes read in about 3, 2 and 2 (Q6).
The first note's opening is re-voiced from “Every founder we audit says…” to “In my experience, nearly every founder says…”, because no audit is claimed yet (Q2). The note itself says the same.
R·01, the Revenue Entropy Index benchmark, shows “In development” with no date. Today's site says “In production · Q4 2026” (Q4).
“New notes · By email when they ship” promises that you'll email notes to people who ask through /contact. Will you?

pages.name: The three field notes
pages.question: “Is my problem really what I think it is, and how would I tell?”

pages.signature: One drawn figure per note, placed where the argument turns.
flags: Lines that claimed audits already run are now your own observation (“In my experience…”), and the 17% note's “strongest single predictor of close” finding is cut (Q2).
Each note carries “Written by Rameez, founder” and keeps its published read time (Q6). The 17% note now says 83% throughout.

Revenue entropy: the figure lets the reader answer the note's three questions about their own company and lights the broken layer. It sits right after the paragraph that asks them, so the questions come twice in a row. Keep it there?
The 17% note: “who else from the account starts visiting, which other roles at the account start engaging” says nearly the same thing twice. Drop the second clause?

pages.name: The System Audit

pages.signature: The ten days drawn to scale, then the three-question gate.
flags: The readout's four parts, and “A written readout and a sequenced rebuild plan” (Q3). A 60-minute readout call isn't mentioned anywhere until you confirm it.
“We reply with times within one working day” (Q3).
Your approved FAQ still says “Ask the founding team”, while other pages say “the founder” (Q1).

questions.title: Who is Kelwin today?
items: Is it you alone, or are there other senior people?
The pages say “Rameez” and “the founder”, and /about says “One architect today”. Your approved homepage CTA and FAQ say “the founding team”. Keep that, or change it to match?
One line of your background on /about, or none?
Confirm “Founder · Lead Narrative Architect” and “Based · London”.
Is the next seat only a Systems Engineer?
questions.def: you alone, as the founder. No background line, and no portrait (rule 6) unless you grant one exception.

questions.title: Track record
items: Have any audits or installs run yet, even ones you can't publish?

If not, the notes' “we audit”, “we've run” and “we see” lines become your own first-person observation, and the 17% note's “strongest single predictor of close” finding is cut, or kept as a stated hypothesis. Which?
questions.def: nothing claimed. The notes speak in your own first person (“In my experience…”), the 17% note's finding is cut, and Reports says “Cleared for publication · None yet”.

questions.title: The readout, and replies
items: Confirm the readout's four parts: narrative readout, channel orchestration map, intelligence gap report, sequenced rebuild plan. /audit and the /reports specimen are built on them.
Is there a 60-minute readout call? It isn't mentioned anywhere until you say so.
Reply times: one working day for audit bookings, two for everything else?
Should bench-list entries go to audit@kelwin.co, or to a careers address?
questions.def: the four parts as listed, no readout call, one and two working days, audit@kelwin.co.

questions.title: The Lab
items: Is it R&D that sharpens the installs, or a product heading to a standalone console?
Which instruments exist today, and at which stage: concept, prototype, used on engagements, or released?
Do install clients get access first? Does the advisory work fund it?
Is the Entropy Index benchmark still on for Q4 2026?
Should The Lab stay top-level in the nav, or move under The Firm, where the footer files it?
questions.def: R&D under the service, nothing used on engagements yet, top-level in the nav.

questions.title: Approved copy that would change
items: (a) Capability header facts: “6-week install, then retainer” becomes “Scoped at the readout”, and “Seven artifacts you own” becomes the layer's own two assets. Yes or no?
(b) Nav item 02.2: “Outbound engine build” becomes “Data pipeline & signal map”. Yes or no?
(c) The Firm and Resources dropdowns: new descriptions (you've never reviewed these; today's are live), including “Get in touch” becoming “Talk to the team”. Yes or no?
(d) A quiet “Inside this layer →” link in each open row of the homepage's System ledger. Today the homepage never links to a capability page. Yes or no?
questions.def: the mockups show (a) and (b) as proposed. (c) and (d) change the nav and the homepage, so they wait for your yes.

questions.title: Your published notes
items: The 17% note's standfirst says 95%, while its body argues from “the other 83%”. Use 83% throughout?
The read times say 6, 5 and 5 minutes, but the notes read in about 3, 2 and 2. They also show on the homepage letter and the evidence door. Correct them, or keep them?
A byline “Written by Rameez, founder” on each note?
questions.def: 83% throughout, the published read times kept until you say, and the byline shown.

questions.title: How you work
items: Is the week on /about (Monday signal review through Thursday kill review, then Friday's written note) how your engagements will run? If not, that section comes out.
Careers: no juniors, pay published with every role, remote-first and London-based?

items: The governing-law jurisdiction for Terms L·08, and the legal entity's name and address, from you or counsel.
